faq.q: What is the origin of Aafia?
faq.a: The form عافية is Arabic and is commonly transliterated Aafiya, Aafia, or similar variants. The word’s Arabic origin is distinct from evidence about how often a particular spelling is used as a personal name.

The Arabic lexical form عافية is Arabic and is associated with health, well-being, or freedom from affliction. Aafia is one Latin-script spelling variant; spelling alone does not establish regional frequency.

faq.q: What is the root of Aafia?
faq.a: The form عافية is conventionally connected with the Arabic root ع ف و (ʿ-f-w). The lexical sense is well-being or soundness; a root label should not be used to claim that the name is Qur’anic.
Aafia is used in Muslim naming contexts and has a positive Arabic lexical sense. That cultural use alone does not establish Qur’anic status or religious prescription.
This record does not establish Aafia as a Qur’anic personal name. An Arabic word with a positive meaning is not, by itself, evidence of a specific Qur’anic reference.

faq.a: عافیہ / عافية کا مفہوم عافیت، صحت اور خیریت سے متعلق ہے۔ نام کے طور پر استعمال اور اس کی علاقائی مقبولیت کے لیے الگ شواہد درکار ہیں۔
